Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
10:42 PM

People in India are moving to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a message. You open any payment app, scan a code or pick a contact, enter your PIN, and the money reaches the other person's bank account in seconds. It works the same whether you are paying a street vendor, a friend or an online shop.

It also helps that almost everyone already has a bank account and a smartphone, and that data got cheap. Shopkeepers of every size, from tea stalls to big stores, can accept payments with just a printed QR code. No card machine, no setup fee. That pushed UPI into places where cards never reached, and once your neighbourhood vendor takes it, carrying cash starts to feel like a hassle.

Here are the main reasons:

It is free and instant. Most person-to-person and small shop payments cost nothing, and money moves 24x7, even on holidays.
It is simple for everyone. One app, one PIN, and a QR code or phone number. Works across banks and apps, so you are never locked in.
It is almost everywhere. From vegetable sellers to rent, bills and online shopping, there is nearly always a way to pay with UPI.
